hero.title: Give AI-built applications a governed home.
hero.description: In a growing number of enterprises, thousands of employees already build working applications with AI coding tools — most of them outside engineering. Creation has scaled; the operating model underneath has not. This is an overview of what that gap looks like, what a governed platform has to do about it, and how the alternatives compare.

whys.title: Creation has scaled. The operating model has not.
whys.body: Roughly 2,500 employees turn ideas into working apps with Claude Code — most of them outside engineering. Those apps need identity, bounded data access, audit trails, and cost attribution that the existing Kubernetes path was never designed to provide at this scale.

whys.title: Every ungoverned week makes the standard harder.
whys.body: Apps that ship without a governed path accumulate shared credentials, unknown data access, and unowned operations. Every week without a standard makes the eventual standard more expensive — you end up migrating a live estate instead of setting a default.

whys.title: Buy the governed layer, not another integration project.
whys.body: Evaluated hands-on across the six lifecycle stages, Vercel is the only end-to-end fit. The alternatives cover parts of the lifecycle and leave the enterprise to assemble, govern, and operate the rest itself.
